candidate_relations.reason: Poikiloderma is a descriptive clinical term for skin changes (atrophy, dyspigmentation, telangiectasia) and represents a morphological feature/component of PPH rather than the complete diagnosis. It lacks the hemangioma/vascular proliferation specificity confirmed by histopathology and IHC (CD34+, CD31+, D2-40-).
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Poikiloderma describes the clinical morphology (atrophic, erythematous-violaceous appearance) that is part of the PPH phenotype, but does not capture the vascular neoplastic component (hemangioma) or the full diagnostic entity of poikilodermatous plaque-like hemangioma

candidate_relations.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
candidate_relations.reason: Histopathology demonstrates band-like vascular proliferation with endothelial cells positive for CD34 and CD31, inconsistent with SCC. There is no mention of keratinocyte atypia, dyskeratosis, or invasive epithelial nests. SCC is a different diagnostic entity entirely.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: SCC is a malignant epithelial neoplasm; the clinical record shows a benign vascular proliferation with no epithelial atypia, no keratinocyte dysplasia, and IHC confirming endothelial (not epithelial) origin

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis (PPH) is a rare and recently described entity; candidates provided are both clearly non-equivalent or only partially related, limiting discriminatory value of the candidate set.
